STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat paper plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: this looks like a small-to-medium paper plate, roughly 18-20 cm.
b) Reference cue: the sausage pieces are about 3-4 cm long and the scrambled egg mound spans roughly 5 sausage-lengths across the plate's right half. The full plate width is about 2.3 to 2.5 sausage lengths... more precisely, the plate diameter is about 5 times the sausage diameter (~2.5 cm), giving ~19 cm.
Reconciled width: about 19 cm (round, area = 0.785 x 19^2 ≈ 283 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: covers roughly 40% of the plate area on the right side (~115 cm²). It is a mound, peak about 2 cm, average about 1 cm. Volume ≈ 115 x 1.0 = 115 ml. Grams = 115 x 0.8 = ~92 g.
- Sautéed spinach with carrot shreds: covers roughly 30% of plate area (~85 cm²), mounded to about 1.5 cm, average ~0.7 cm. Volume ≈ 60 ml. Cooked leafy greens density 0.6 → ~36 g. Oil/dressing sheen included, add a small amount: ~40 g total.
- Sausage links: 3 pieces (two visible whole-ish, one partly under), each about 35-40 g cooked, about 100 g total.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the egg and greens are flat-to-mounded with no deep base layer. No hidden base beyond what is counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Scrambled egg (with some butter/oil): ~150 kcal/100 g
- Cooked spinach with carrot and oil: ~50 kcal/100 g
- Pork/beef sausage, cooked: ~300 kcal/100 g

Totals: egg 92 g ≈ 138 kcal; greens 40 g ≈ 20 kcal; sausage 100 g ≈ 300 kcal. Total ≈ 200 g, ≈ 460 kcal.
